incidents.name: Rari Fuse (Pool reentrancy)
incidents.notes: Fuse pool cEther (fToken) exitMarket/borrow cross-function reentrancy via .call value transfer before state update.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2022-04/Rari_exp.sol names the same victim as fETH-127. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 14685453, 2022-04-30T12:00:00Z). The victim 0x26267e41CeCa7C8E0f143554Af707336f27Fa051 is a Fuse CEtherDelegator (verified) created at block 13673508, 2021-11-23T22:34:04Z. It emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event; its fallback reads the implementation from storage slot 0 (it delegatecalls sload(0) with selector 0x1db78944 = `_prepare()`, Fuse's auto-upgrade hook, then delegatecalls sload(0) with the original calldata), and `implementation()` (0x5c60da1b) returns that same slot. Two independent checks show the pointer never moved: eth_getLogs for Compound's NewImplementation(address,address) over [creation, incident] returns exactly one event, the 0x0 -> 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf write in the creation block, and a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on slot 0 finds it unchanged since creation. The implementation 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf (deployed 2021-10-01T07:05:21Z) itself contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes, so it is a leaf. Fuse's `_prepare()` auto-upgrade never fired for this market and the deployment basis is exact.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis (independent re-check of the existing note). Slot 0 held 0xd77e28a1b9a9cfe1fc2eee70e391c05d25853cbf at all 25 sample points across [13673508, 14685453], and the only NewImplementation(address,address) event on the delegator is the 0x0 -> 0xd77e28a1 write in its creation block 13673508.

exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (block 14684814): the exit-fee reentrancy drain of Fuse pool 127 fETH 0x26267e41ceca7c8e0f143554af707336f27fa051 (this row's victim), the tx DeFiHackLabs reproduces and CertiK's analysis cites; the wider incident drained ~7 pools across sequential txs from the same attacker
